minor.issue: winner_email may return null even when the pool has API-created entries. Root cause: seeded pools set tickets_sold to non-zero phantom values (e.g. Amazon=187) without inserting matching entry documents. The draw picks winning_ticket uniformly in [1, tickets_sold] and looks it up in entries[*].ticket_numbers — if the chosen number falls in the phantom seeded range, no winner is found. Review_request expects winner_email to match the entry holder. Either (a) seed pools with tickets_sold=0 and let real entries fill them, or (b) restrict winning_ticket to only ticket numbers that exist in db.entries for that competition.

Cannot reproduce the '0 entries -> 400' branch with the current seed because every seeded pool has tickets_sold > 0 from start. Code path exists and is correct (line 265-266 server.py), test SKIPPED. Consider seeding at least one pool with tickets_sold=0 for full coverage.

rca_of_issue: Issue: POST /api/admin/draws/{pid} can return winner_email=null even when the pool has real entries. Reproduction: 1) GET /api/pools — pick any seeded pool (e.g. Amazon tickets_sold=187). 2) POST /api/entries with qty=1 (now tickets_sold=188, but only ticket #188 has an owner). 3) POST /api/admin/draws/{pid} as admin. 4) Random pick uniformly samples [1,188]; with probability 187/188 the chosen ticket has no owner -> winner_email=null. Mitigation options: (a) Modify run_draw to draw from the actual list of issued ticket_numbers stored in entries (cryptographically pick one entry, then pick a ticket within it), or (b) Change seed_pools to start every pool with tickets_sold=0 so the draw space equals the entries space. Option (a) is more product-correct.
